prompt.context: Tristar is a large international manufacturer of electronics, home appliances, software, and biotech products. Their home appliance line (refrigerators, washers & dryers, microwaves) has been very successful in the United States, mostly through a B2C model: they get their products into retailers like Best Buy, Sears, Home Depot, etc. Tristar management has set aggressive revenue targets for the coming year, and the home appliance business unit director has some concerns about meeting them.
prompt.question: She has asked your firm for help in evaluating a new opportunity: B2B sales, specifically the home builders market. Tristar would sell appliances to builders, who would then install them in their new units. Sales could also occur for home remodeling. Should Tristar enter the B2B home builders market?

clarifying_info.q: Who are the current competitors in the home builders appliance market?
clarifying_info.a: The builders market is split 50/50 between two competitors: GE and Whirlpool.

clarifying_info.q: Does Tristar have existing relationships with any distributors?
clarifying_info.a: Tristar has strong sales throughout the US and has existing relationships with large distributors.

clarifying_info.q: How does selling to builders differ from selling to retailers?
clarifying_info.a: With a retailer like Best Buy the firm simply supplies sufficient inventory, whereas in the builders market deliveries must occur on a particular day to a particular building site.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue targets vs. current projections?
clarifying_info.a: That information will be shared via exhibit shortly.

exhibits.title: Retail Sales Opportunity
exhibits.shows: A table of Tristar's expected 2017 retail sales versus its ~30% market share target across five major retail channels (Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowe's, Sears, Others), plus a Total column.

exhibits.title: Builders Market Data
exhibits.shows: New home price and cost breakdown assumptions, and a table of expected appliance spend per remodeling project type (Minor, Major, New Addition) split by Single Family and Multi-Family.

exhibits.title: Distribution Channels
exhibits.shows: A diagram of distribution channels from Manufacturer to end builders, with nodes for Large Distributors, Small Builder/Distributors, Large Builder/Distributors, and Large Builders. Lines indicate which relationships Tristar currently has.

exhibits.title: Distribution Market Share
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the percentage of the home builders appliance market attributable to each distribution/builder segment (Small Builder/Distributors, Large Builder/Distributors, Large Builders).

data.note: See image for exact percentage breakdown; Builder/Distributors combined account for approximately 80% of the market

framework: 1. Market: (a) Competition — current market split 50/50 between GE and Whirlpool; what market share is realistically capturable? (b) Risks — housing market outlook and volatility; is this a reliable revenue stream?
2. Company: (a) Production capacity — can Tristar meet additional demand? (b) Distribution capacity — can existing logistics serve point-of-construction delivery requirements?
3. Revenues: (a) Volume — size and growth of the home builders market (new builds + remodeling) (b) Pricing — can Tristar command competitive pricing in this new channel?
4. Costs (secondary): Changes to distribution model; additional administrative overhead for B2B channel.

questions.prompt: From Exhibit 1, what is the revenue gap between Tristar's target and expected 2017 sales? Can this gap be closed through the existing retail channel?
questions.guidance: Candidate should subtract expected sales from target: $4,600M - $3,460M = $1,140M gap (~$1.1B). Tristar has ~23% market share currently and is targeting ~30%. Candidate should note this is an ambitious expansion in a saturated market and likely cannot be closed through retail alone, motivating exploration of the B2B channel.

math.setup: Tristar target retail revenue minus expected 2017 retail sales

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the total size of the home builders appliance market (new builds + remodeling).
questions.guidance: Candidate must derive construction costs from new home price, then apply the 2% appliance cost. For remodeling, candidate uses the provided spend table multiplied by project counts and purchase rates. Strong candidates will show structured mental math and note that remodeling is the larger segment.

math.setup: New Homes: Average price $300,000. Builder margin 6%, land 15%, other non-construction 10% => construction costs = 100% - 6% - 15% - 10% = 69% ~ 70% of price. Appliances = 2% of construction costs. Assume ~1M new home starts per year. Remodeling: sum rows of project count x purchase rate x avg spend.
steps: Remodeling rows: Single Family Minor: 1,400k x 25% x $2,000 = $700M; Single Family Major: 900k x 80% x $5,000 = $3,600M; Single Family New Addition: 100k x 100% x $8,000 = $800M; Multi-Family Minor: 900k x 0% = $0; Multi-Family Major: 1,000k x 100% x $2,500 = $2,500M
math.answer: Total market ~$11.8B; capturing just 10% (~$1.18B) would close the revenue gap.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, what distribution options does Tristar have to reach the home builders market? What are the tradeoffs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that Tristar already has relationships with Large Distributors who serve both Small and Large Builder/Distributors, so it can reach those segments quickly via existing channels. It can also build a direct relationship with Large Builders, capturing more value but requiring a different logistics operation (day-specific, site-specific delivery). The key insight is that the B2B distribution model is fundamentally different from retail replenishment.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 4, which distribution segment should Tristar prioritize, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Builder/Distributors (small and large combined) account for ~80% of the market. Given Tristar needs only 10% market share to meet targets, focusing on the distributor/builder segment — accessible through existing large distributor relationships — is the most efficient and lowest-risk path. Direct relationships with Large Builders could be a phase-two initiative.

math.setup: Market share needed: 10% of $11.8B = $1.18B. Builder/Distributors = ~80% of market.
steps: Remainder needed from large builders direct or other segments
math.answer: Prioritize Builder/Distributors segment (80% of market); accessible via existing distributor relationships and sufficient to approach the revenue target.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors and considerations will determine the feasibility of entering the home builders market?

categories.name: Production Capacity
ideas: Can current manufacturing scale meet incremental B2B volume?
Lead times for new production capacity if needed
Inventory buffering requirements for site-specific deliveries

categories.name: Distribution Model
ideas: Point-of-construction delivery requires day- and site-specific logistics — fundamentally different from retail replenishment
Need to build or partner for last-mile delivery to job sites
Potential conflicts with existing retail channel partners

categories.name: Competitive Landscape
ideas: GE and Whirlpool split the market 50/50 and are entrenched
Competitive response risk (price war, exclusive contracts with builders)
Tristar is of comparable size — credible challenger

categories.name: Revenue & Pricing
ideas: Pricing pressure in B2B vs. B2C retail
Volume discounts expected by large builders
Revenue timing may differ (project-based vs. continuous retail flow)

categories.name: Upfront Investment
ideas: Potential need for dedicated account management

categories.name: Market Risk
ideas: Regulatory changes affecting new home starts

recommendation: Tristar should pursue the B2B home builders market opportunity as a means to close the ~$1.1B revenue gap between targets and expected 2017 sales.
The total builders market is ~$11.8B; capturing just 10% would fill the gap. The market is concentrated (GE and Whirlpool 50/50) but Tristar is of similar scale and is a credible new entrant.
Priority should be on the Builder/Distributor segment (~80% of market), accessible through Tristar's existing large-distributor relationships, minimizing upfront channel investment.
risks: Investment required to build a new distribution model capable of day- and site-specific delivery
Risk of diverting management attention and resources from the core retail business
Housing market volatility could make this an unreliable revenue stream
next_steps: Study the competitive landscape to determine which geographic markets to target first and how to set competitive pricing
Analyze distribution channels in detail to map the best path to establishing or deepening relationships with Builder/Distributors
Assess production and logistics capacity to confirm ability to fulfill B2B volume without disrupting retail supply
